examples.en: The snake came closer, flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 난로 불길이 널름거리는 걸 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the flames licking in the stove for a while.
The puppy waits for a treat, licking its lips.
The lizard flicked its tongue in and out, which was fascinating.
Flames began to lick up over the roof.
The baby sticking its tongue in and out is cute.

explain: 혀나 불길이 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. 작은말은 '날름거리다'예요. 물결이 크게 흔들리는 '너울거리다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes a tongue or flames quickly darting out and back in. The smaller-sounding version is '날름거리다'. Don't confuse it with '너울거리다', which is about large, soft waving.

examples.en: I twirl spaghetti around my fork and eat it.

examples.ko: 아기가 이불을 돌돌 말고 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is sleeping rolled up in the blanket.
I rolled up the poster and put it in the tube.

examples.ko: 머리카락을 손가락에 돌돌 감는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of twirling my hair around my finger.

examples.ko: 김밥 속을 넣고 김을 돌돌 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Put the filling in and roll up the seaweed, please.

examples.ko: 실을 돌돌 감아서 서랍에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Wind the thread up and put it in the drawer.

explain: 가늘거나 얇은 것을 둥글게 여러 번 마는 모양이에요. 보통 '말다', '감다'와 함께 써요. '둘둘'은 같은 모양이지만 더 크고 두툼한 것에 쓰는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes thin or slim things being rolled or wound round several times. It usually goes with '말다' or '감다'. '둘둘' describes the same motion but feels more suited to bigger, thicker things.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped myself up in the blanket and slept.
I wound the scarf around my neck several times.
I wrapped the gift up in newspaper.
I wound tissue around my hand and wiped it.
Please wind the rope around the stick.

examples.ko: 아이가 담요를 둘둘 말고 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sitting wrapped up in a blanket.

explain: 길거나 넓은 것을 여러 번 감거나 마는 모양이고, '말다', '감다', '싸다'와 잘 같이 써요. '돌돌'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이고, '둘둘'은 더 크고 두툼한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes wrapping or rolling something long or wide several times, and goes well with '말다', '감다' and '싸다'. '돌돌' feels smaller and lighter, while '둘둘' feels bigger and thicker.

examples.ko: 분가를 하려면 먼저 집부터 구해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to move out, you first need to find a place.
My older brother is preparing to move out this year.
Even after moving out, I visit my parents often.
What was your reason for deciding to move out?

examples.ko: 분가는 보통 결혼할 때 많이 해요.
examples.en: People usually move out of the family home when they get married.
The newlyweds got a small home when they moved out on their own.

explain: 결혼 같은 일로 부모님이나 큰집에서 나와 따로 살림을 차리는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '이사'와 달리 가족에서 독립해 새 가정을 이룬다는 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 일상에서는 '독립'이라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 반대로 다시 합치는 건 '합가'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means leaving your parents' or the main family's home, usually after marriage, to set up your own household. Unlike plain '이사' (moving), it carries the feeling of becoming a separate family. In daily talk '독립' is more common now, and the opposite, living together again, is '합가'.

examples.ko: 모기가 귀 옆에서 윙윙거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mosquito buzzed next to my ear, so I couldn't sleep.
Bees are buzzing around the flowers.
The fan whirred all night.

examples.ko: 윙윙거리는 소리 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't concentrate because of the buzzing sound.
A fly is buzzing around over the food.
I get annoyed every time a mosquito buzzes.

explain: 벌, 모기, 선풍기, 기계처럼 낮고 가늘게 이어지는 소리를 낼 때 써요. 귀에서 윙윙 소리가 나는 느낌을 말할 때도 '귀가 윙윙거려요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes the low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes, fans and machines. It is also used for ringing in the ears, as in '귀가 윙윙거려요'.

examples.ko: 아기 이름 작명은 할머니께서 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother chose the baby's name for us.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 작명 센스가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This shop has a really great sense for naming things.
Naming is hard, so I've been agonizing over it for days.
We got the baby's name from a naming house.
We picked the puppy's name from a naming contest.

examples.ko: 게임 캐릭터 작명에 두 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Naming my game character took a whole two hours.

explain: 사람 이름뿐 아니라 가게, 제품, 반려동물 이름을 지을 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '이름 짓기'라고도 하고, '작명 센스'는 이름을 재치 있게 잘 지었을 때 칭찬하는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used not only for people's names but also for shops, products and pets. In everyday talk you can also say '이름 짓기'. '작명 센스' is a common way to praise someone for coming up with a clever name.

examples.en: I reorganized the order of the story and rewrote it.
We decided to rearrange the office seating.

examples.ko: 사건 현장을 재구성해 보니 단서가 보였어요.
examples.en: When we reconstructed the scene, clues appeared.

examples.ko: 수업 내용을 재구성한 자료를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: They handed out materials with the lesson content restructured.
The presentation order needs to be reorganized.
The reorganizing took a lot of time.

explain: 이미 있는 내용이나 구조를 다시 짜 맞춘다는 느낌이에요. 글, 수업 자료, 사건 설명 등에 두루 쓰고, 보통 '재구성하다' 형태로 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of putting existing content or structure together again. It is used broadly for writing, lesson materials and accounts of events, and is usually said as '재구성하다'.

examples.en: I changed the order of the presentation and reorganized the content.

examples.ko: 선생님이 수업 자료를 학생 수준에 맞게 재구성하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher reorganized the lesson materials to fit the students' level.

examples.ko: 이 글을 시간 순서대로 재구성해 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we try rearranging this text in chronological order?

examples.ko: 사건 현장 사진으로 그날 상황을 재구성하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are reconstructing what happened that day using photos from the scene.

examples.ko: 소설을 영화로 재구성하면서 결말이 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: As the novel was reworked into a movie, the ending changed a lot.
Some suggested restructuring the department.

explain: 이미 있는 것을 순서나 구조를 바꿔서 새로 짜 맞출 때 써요. 글, 수업, 팀, 사건 과정 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. '다시 재구성하다'는 '재'가 겹쳐서 어색하니 '재구성하다'만 쓰세요.
explain_en: Use it when you take something that already exists and rearrange its order or structure into something new. It goes well with texts, lessons, teams and event reconstructions. '다시 재구성하다' repeats the idea of 'again' and sounds awkward, so just say '재구성하다'.
